title: GTI Perspectives on Cancer: A Systemic and Evolutionary Framework
content: This paper introduces a novel axiomatic framework for understanding cancer not as a pathological anomaly, but as a systemic adaptive response to existential failure. Drawing from the General Theory of Innovation (GTI), cancer is reframed as a last-resort structural behavior enacted by systems that can no longer sustain equilibrium.  The framework integrates systems theory, failure dynamics, and functional emergence to offer an innovative hypothesis of disease onset as a structurally lawful process of adaptation.The work contributes to cross-disciplinary discourse in innovation theory, complexity science, and health systems analysis. It provides conceptual scaffolding for improved diagnostics, early detection, and systemic intervention strategies—particularly in cases where conventional models struggle to account for emergent disease behavior. This paper was developed in collaboration with an AI assistant (ChatGPT, OpenAI) used for iterative drafting, editing, and conceptual exploration.
